newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia banks SKB and UBK sign cooperation accord.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia banks SKB and UBK sign cooperation accord.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said on Tuesday it had signed a contract last week to cooperate with bank UBK.
"The managements of banks SKB and UBK (last) Wednesday signed a (preliminary) contract about forming a bank group of SKB bank," SKB said in a statement.
Both banks declined any immediate further comment but said they would hold a joint news conference on Thursday at 0900 GMT to detail their cooperation plans.
Among Slovenia's 28 banks, SKB holds an 11.2 percent market share, while UBK has a share of less than 0.9 percent.
UBK announced its merger plans late last year, while SKB said in March it planned to increase its market share in Slovenia to about 16 percent by the year 2000.
SKB's net profit in 1996 rose to 1.79 billion tolars from 713 million, while balance sheet assets were up to 208.3 billion tolars from 178.6 billion.
UBK's preliminary net profit for 1996 slumped to 11.7 million tolars from 120 million in 1995, while balance sheet assets fell to 13.2 billion tolars from 13.9 billion.
Analysts have forecast a wave of banking mergers in Slovenia in the next few years as the sector tries to reduce costs in order to fight off foreign competition.
Parliament is expected to pass a law later this year enabling foreign banks to establish branches in the tiny Alpine republic. Currently international banks can only set up subsidiaries.
At 0930 GMT shares of SKB were up 0.6 percent to 48,820 tolars, while UBK jumped 3.28 percent to 6,300 tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
